subject: CardioSys: deployment slate comparison (Private vs Dedicated) + mutual action plan

Subject: Private vs Dedicated comparison for CardioSys pilot

Hi Irene —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re moving fast on the pilot for our clinical decision-support feature and procurement asked me to get a clear recommendation: what footprint should we commit to for an initial 12-week pilot if we choose Private (VPC, air-gapped option) vs Dedicated (Redwood-managed reserved GPUs)? Key asks from our side:

- A short table with recommended node counts, expected p99 token latency, and burst-to-commit options for both hosting modes.
- Any notable differences in onboarding time and evidence needed for compliance (SOC2, KMS, audit logs).
- A draft mutual action plan and a ballpark committed monthly cost range so procurement can triage to finance.

We’re sensitive to data residency — CardioSys will require private networking for PHI ingestion if we choose Private. Happy to hop on a quick call. Can Karthik or someone share sizing guidance for a 50 qps peak with ~256-token average responses using a 30B LLM?

Thanks,
Luke

Subject: Re: Private vs Dedicated comparison for CardioSys pilot

Luke —

Appreciate the clear ask. I’m looping in Karthik (inference & deal engineering) and Marissa (solutions lead) to put together a concise comparison and an M.A.P. draft. High level summary up front:

- Dedicated (reserved Redwood capacity): fastest time-to-launch (~2–3 weeks), predictable throughput for sustained 50 qps, simpler KMS integration (handled by Redwood via customer key) but no on-prem air-gap. Recommended initial slate: 8x A100-80GB equivalent (or 12x A10 if using cheaper accelerator mix) to reliably hit 50 qps with 256-token average and to maintain p99 < 300ms on typical LLMs in our catalog.

- Private (VPC / customer-managed private control plane): required for PHI/data residency. Expect longer lead time (~4–6 weeks) for infra setup, network validation, and SOC2 evidence handoff. For equivalent latency and headroom we recommend 6–8 private nodes with NVLink-backed GPUs (depends on model quantization). Private gets you stronger network isolation and complete control over logs.

I’m attaching a short one-pager (Redwood_Private_vs_Dedicated_Overview.pdf) and a draft MA P to this thread. Karthik: can you add the detailed capacity workbook (GPU mixing, quantization suggestions) and a quick notes section on fallback policies (burst to dedicated if private nodes need to scale)? Marissa: I’ll need your help on procurement language/term windows.

Next steps proposed:
1) Karthik to send sizing workbook and a recommended initial configuration by EOD tomorrow.
2) Redwood to supply SOC2 artifact checklist + sample DocuSign statements for KMS access.
3) CardioSys to confirm preferred hosting posture (Private vs Dedicated) and desired pilot start window (target week of Apr 12).

Happy to jump on a 30-minute alignment call — propose Tue 3/16 10am PT if that works.

Best,
Irene

Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private vs Dedicated comparison for CardioSys pilot — capacity workbook attached

Luke / Irene / team —

Per Irene’s note, attached is a compact workbook and two config stubs. Highlights (tailored to 30B-class model, FP16 or 4-bit quantized path):

- Workload assumptions: 50 qps peak, average request 256 tokens, 10% long tails (>= 1024 tokens).
- Dedicated recommendation (lowest friction): 8x A100-80GB equiv. baseline. Headroom for burst traffic (1.5x) via autoscaling / reserved burst lanes; expected sustained token throughput ~1.2M tokens/min. Estimated p99: ~250–350ms (model dependent).

- Private recommendation: 6 nodes with NVLink (A100-80GB equiv) if you require strict data residency and full network control. Because Private typically runs with slightly more conservative batching and isolated scheduling, plan for 1.2–1.4x the node count vs an equivalent Redwood-managed reserved pool if you want identical p99 SLAs. So suggest sizing at 7x for parity if you want cushion for long-tail requests.

- Cost delta: rough monthly committed cost for Dedicated (8x A100 equiv) ~ $XXXk–$YYYk; Private (6–7 nodes) ~ $YYYk–$ZZZk plus one-time deployment fees for on-prem/VPC package and a 1–2 week validation window. (I’ll populate a more precise per-GPU cost ladder in the workbook.)

- Fallback policy: suggest an automated policy to route non-sensitive traffic to a cost-tiered model in hosted Redwood and keep PHI-bound calls on Private. Also recommend a canary window and automatic fallback to Dedicated pool if Private nodes enter degraded state.

Attachments: CardioSys_capacity_workbook.csv, inference-config.yaml, Draft_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx

Let me know if you want me to convert the workbook to a one-pager for procurement.

-Karthik

- Procurement asked for the SOC2 artifact list and the KMS DocuSign template you mentioned. Can you send those and the one-page cost ladder for the two options (we only need the ballpark numbers to route to Finance today)?
- Next steps: we will (1) confirm internal PO timeline (target week of 3/29), (2) share the signed M.A.P., and (3) schedule the network validation window during the pilot prep week.

We’re good with Tue 3/16 10am PT — Luke will join from the infra side. If you prefer, we can keep that call to technical alignment and handle procurement separately.

Appreciate the help.
Alice
